comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C15-C25. Both evaluations support the basic characterization showing DKO cells are resistant to apoptotic and necrotic stimuli using multiple complementary assays (MultiTox-Fluor, annexin V/PI, caspase inhibition, EM). Reviewers do not challenge these fundamental observations.

Perfect agreement on claims C29-C30. Both evaluations support the in vivo cardiac I-R injury and MI data showing protective effects of Bax/Bak deletion. Peer reviewers focus concerns on mechanistic interpretation of in vitro experiments rather than challenging these in vivo findings.

Perfect agreement on claims C39-C40. Both evaluations support the alamethicin and osmotic control experiments. Reviewers specifically requested these controls and acknowledge they demonstrate DKO mitochondria can swell under non-MPTP conditions, ruling out general structural abnormalities.

Disagreement on claims C68-C70. OpenEval finds mitoplast experiments conclusively demonstrate Bax/Bak do not affect inner membrane MPTP. Peer reviewers acknowledge MPTP occurs in mitoplasts but request additional non-MPTP swelling agents (valinomycin) to confirm specificity, expressing uncertainty about whether resistance is MPTP-specific or a general outer membrane property.

Agreement on claims C64-C66. Both evaluations support the patch clamp data showing reduced outer membrane conductance in DKO mitochondria and restoration with rBax. Reviewers do not challenge these direct biophysical measurements, though they question downstream mechanistic interpretations.

Disagreement on claims C54-C57. OpenEval finds outer membrane permeabilization experiments (rBax, gossypol, digitonin, tetanolysin) support the model. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, wanting to determine if this is specifically MPTP-related or a general property of outer membrane permeability independent of MPTP opening mechanism.

Disagreement on claims C31-C36 (mitochondrial swelling assays). OpenEval finds consistent evidence across multiple tissues and MPTP inducers strongly supports Bax/Bak role. Peer reviewers acknowledge the observation is interesting but express uncertainty, stating 'the link with MPTP-dependent swelling is therefore an interpretation that must be confirmed by additional experiments.'

Disagreement on claims C50-C53 (EM morphology). OpenEval finds EM data provides strong structural support for functional swelling assays. Peer reviewers' uncertainty about MPTP-specificity extends to interpretation of these morphological observations, questioning whether resistance to swelling/rupture is specifically MPTP-related.

Disagreement on main conclusions C1-C4. OpenEval finds converging evidence strongly supports that Bax/Bak affect outer membrane permeability independently of oligomerization. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about the MPTP-specific interpretation, noting 'the interpretation of such may change depending on the outcome of suggested experiments.'

Disagreement on claims C48-C49 (non-oligomerizing mutants). OpenEval finds mutant data critical for demonstrating oligomerization-independent function in necrosis. Peer reviewers do not directly comment but their overall uncertainty about MPTP-specificity applies to mechanistic interpretation of how Bax functions, affecting confidence in the oligomerization-independence claim.
